title: Twice as Fast? Kinetic Energy Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A slow ball just taps the pads. A fast ball stings. Aarav faces a ball at 10 m/s, then one at 20 m/s. Twice the speed, but does it hit twice as hard? No: it carries four times the energy. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 5, Work, Energy and Power) for NCERT, CBSE, ISC and PUC students, plus JEE and NEET, we find out exactly why.

On a live motion notebook a 4 N force pushes a 2 kg cart along a smooth track: after 1 m, 4 m and 9 m it moves at 2, 4 and 6 m/s, with a live readout, a K vs v graph and a slow-mo replay. We derive K = 1/2 mv^2 step by step from W = Fd, F = ma and v^2 = 2ad, and write it as K = p^2/2m. Side by side: double the mass vs double the speed, then why K is never negative. Two pause-and-think questions, a worked cricket ball example, the exam trap about equal momentum, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.
